acceptanceCriteria: internal/testvalidity reports an invalid-severity finding for expect { <name> } when <name> is a subject or let invoked in an enclosing before or let! of the same or an outer group, naming that before/let! file:line; synthetic spec fixtures cover subject, named subject, let, and a negative where the before is in a sibling group
expect { described_class.new.perform } and expect { <name> } with no memoizing ancestor are not reported
The test-validity verdict exposes the finding so a proof binding refuses the example; a test covers the refusal
Numbered requirements and traceability rows land in the test-validity spec; the zero-coverage-of-target-lines ask is filed as a separate ticket if not delivered
body: GitHub issue #1124. In RSpec, expect { subject } returns the memoized value when an enclosing before (or let!) already invoked subject, so change/raise_error/have_received block expectations are vacuous and not_to change always passes. Observed in a real suite: four examples bound as requirement proof all passed while exercising nothing. internal/testvalidity has no Ruby/RSpec rule today (only JS/Playwright and Go families), so this needs a Ruby spec reader scoped to describe/context nesting, subject/let/let!/before declarations and expect-block bodies. Expected: an invalid-severity finding naming the memoizing before/let! file:line, exposed in the test-validity verdict so callers can refuse the example as proof. Related optional ask: expectations whose target lines had zero coverage in that example's run (needs per-example coverage input).
title: test-validity: flag RSpec block expectations on a subject/let already memoized by an outer before (#1124)
